stories.headline: Iran and Oman Discuss Strait of Hormuz Framework Amid Ongoing Conflict
stories.body:
Iranian and Omani foreign ministers discussed a framework agreement in Tehran [c6]. They spoke about setting up a temporary shipping corridor in the Strait of Hormuz [c6]. They also discussed clearing naval mines from the passage [c6].

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Tehran and Oman agreed on arrangements for the strait [c4]. They said the two sides agreed on sharing the waterway [c4]. They also agreed on sharing its revenues [c4].

Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi spoke about reopening the strait [c7]. He said the Strait of Hormuz will only reopen in exchange for clear actions [c7]. He said the war must end [c7]. He said the blockade must be lifted [c7]. He also said the situation in Yemen must be resolved [c7].

Qatar's prime minister is scheduled to travel to Tehran soon [c1]. He aims to restart diplomatic negotiations between Iran and the United States [c1].

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian commented on the war [c9]. He said that the war must end at some point [c9]. He added that Iran still negotiates from a position of strength [c9].

US President Donald Trump said that the war with Iran will continue [c8]. He said it will carry on for as long as necessary [c8].

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu expressed doubt about peace talks [c5]. He said he doubted negotiations could produce an agreement [c5]. He said this was due to Iran's current leadership [c5].

Shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has dropped severely. Ship-tracking data showed that about 5 million barrels of oil per day passed through the strait on Monday [c2]. Before February 28, roughly 20 million barrels per day passed through the passage [c2].

Data from ship tracker Kpler showed a similar slowdown [c10]. Kpler reported that only 112 oil and gas tankers passed through the strait between August 1 and August 19 [c10].

Safety in the waterway has also worsened. The UN's International Maritime Organization recorded 70 incidents in the Strait of Hormuz [c3]. These incidents occurred since February 28 [c3]. The organization reported that these events resulted in the deaths of 19 seafarers [c3].

vocab.meaning: people who work on ships at sea

stories.headline: United States Imposes New Tariffs on Canadian Imports
stories.body:
The United States imposed new 50 percent tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian imports [c12]. Trade negotiations collapsed before the US announced the decision [c12].

US President Donald Trump said in an interview that it was time to teach Canada a lesson [c11]. He said Canada cannot continue its actions [c11]. Trump also announced 50 percent tariffs on Canadian autos and auto parts [c14]. Those tariffs will take effect on January 1 [c14].

US Vice President JD Vance spoke at a rally in Maine [c16]. He claimed that Canada and China are the two worst countries regarding trade policy [c16]. In a leaked audio recording, Vance called Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney a sweet guy who tries to out-tough Trump [c19].

Carney said that Canada had been attacked [c15]. Canada announced retaliatory tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on about $20 billion of US goods [c17]. These tariffs target US steel, dairy products, appliances, and farm equipment [c15].

Canadian Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne said Canada will match US tariffs dollar for dollar [c18]. The retaliatory tariffs will take effect on September 8 [c13]. Annual trade between the two nations totals over $872 billion [c20].

vocab.meaning: done in response to an attack or injury
taxes placed on goods coming into a country

stories.headline: Hospital Fire in Islamabad Kills 14 Newborn Infants
stories.body:
A fire at a hospital maternity ward in Islamabad killed 14 newborn infants [c21]. The disaster occurred in the mother and child unit at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences [c21].

Rescue officials said the fire started around 6:45 a.m. [c24]. An air-conditioning unit compressor exploded inside the nursery [c24]. Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal said oxygen canisters inside the ward intensified the flames [c27].

Hospital spokesperson Dr. Aneeza Jalil said 15 babies were in the ward when the fire broke out [c26]. She said a doctor saved one baby [c26]. Kamal confirmed that at least 14 babies died in the fire [c25].

PIMS Executive Director Rana Imran Sikander spoke about safety at the facility [c22]. He said the ward door was manned rather than locked to prevent baby theft [c22].

Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif suspended Federal Health Secretary Aslam Ghauri after the hospital fire [c23].

vocab.meaning: related to motherhood or giving birth
a machine that squeezes gas into a smaller space

stories.headline: Meta Reaches Multi-Billion Dollar Settlement With US States Over Teen Safety
stories.body:
Meta agreed to pay billions of dollars to settle lawsuits from US states over youth safety [c28]. France 24 reported that Meta agreed to pay $17 billion to settle claims from 47 states [c29]. Livemint reported a $16.68 billion settlement with 29 states [c33]. Al Jazeera put the total settlement figure at up to $17.1 billion [c28].

The lawsuits accused Meta of causing social media addiction and harm to teenagers [c29]. They also made claims regarding child data collection [c33].

Under the agreement, Meta will add daily time limits on Instagram and Facebook [c30]. It will also pause notifications during daytime school hours [c30]. Meta proposed a two-hour daily limit for users under 18 years old [c31].

Meta said 30 percent of the payment depends on other companies [c32]. YouTube and TikTok must implement matching daily limits and safety features for Meta to pay that portion [c32].

Meta previously faced legal penalties in New Mexico [c34]. A jury ordered Meta to pay $375 million in March [c34]. A judge ordered Meta to pay $567 million on August 6 [c34].

vocab.meaning: an official agreement that ends a legal dispute
depending on certain rules or events

stories.headline: Syrian Democratic Forces Dissolve to Join State Military
stories.body:
The Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces dissolved after merging with the Syrian state military [c35]. The group officially announced its dissolution on August 25, 2026 [c37].

SDF leader Mazloum Abdi made the announcement during a speech in Damascus [c38]. He spoke at the presidential palace [c38].

The group was founded in 2015 [c36]. It controlled large areas of northern Syria before the merger [c36].

Under the agreement, SDF fighters will join the Syrian army under the Defence Ministry [c39]. The Asayish security forces will join the Interior Ministry [c39].

SDF official Abdulkarim Omar spoke about the Women's Protection Units [c40]. He said the unit proposed joining the Interior Ministry as a specialized counterterrorism force [c40].

The Turkish government commented on the dissolution [c41]. Turkey said the move is crucial for strengthening Syrian state authority and stability [c41].

vocab.meaning: the official ending or closing of an organization
actions taken to prevent or fight terrorism

stories.headline: Flash Floods Strike Nepal and Cause Damage Near Tibet Border
stories.body:
Severe flash floods struck Nepal and damaged border areas near Tibet on August 26, 2026 [c43]. Flooding occurred at Trishuli in Nuwakot district [c43].

Survivors described the moment their homes were swept away in a landslide [c54].

The disaster destroyed key infrastructure along the border. The flood destroyed Miteri Sanghu, which is also called Friendship Bridge [c53]. The bridge crossed the Lhende/Koshi river at the border between Nepal and China [c53].

Hundreds of 40-foot shipping containers were parked along the Timure riverbanks [c52]. Floodwaters dislodged the containers and swept them downstream [c52].

The Rasuwagadhi Himalayan corridor suffered severe disruption [c50]. The route has served as a major trans-Himalayan trade passage for over 260 years [c50]. More than 6,500 Chinese electric vehicles passed into Nepal through this crossing in 2025-26 [c51].

Many foreign travelers were affected by the flooding across the region. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese confirmed that 34 Australians were missing in Nepal [c42].

Indian tourists and pilgrims were also trapped. A 32-member tour group from Kolkata became untraceable after the floods [c55].

At least 57 pilgrims from Tamil Nadu were stranded in Nepal [c44]. A Kumbakonam-based company and a Nepal-based firm organized their trip [c47]. About 21 of these pilgrims found shelter at a Nepal border police outpost [c48].

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay ordered coordinated rescue efforts [c45]. He directed Tamil Nadu House in New Delhi to assist the pilgrims [c45]. The Tamil Nadu state government also established 24-hour toll-free helplines for families [c46].

Isha Foundation founder Sadhguru Jaggi Vasudev provided details about another large tour group on August 26 [c49]. He said 495 people from their tour returned safely [c49]. He added that 743 people were in Tibet and 148 were in Nepal [c49].

vocab.meaning: knocked or forced out of position
unable to be found or located

stories.headline: India and China Announce Eight-Point Consensus on Border Management
stories.body:
India and China announced an eight-point consensus on border management following high-level talks in Beijing [c56]. Indian National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi co-chaired the special representatives meeting [c56]. Doval also met Chinese Vice-President Han Zheng before delegation talks [c65].

Wang Yi used the phrase "Dragon-Elephant Dance" to describe cooperation despite differences [c66].

The two nations agreed to establish two new military meeting points [c57]. They also agreed to open two new border military hotlines [c57]. In addition, they agreed to reopen three designated border trading points [c63].

India thanked China for expanding batches for the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra pilgrimage [c62]. Both sides agreed to hold the 26th round of talks in India in 2027 [c58].

The special talks mechanism began in 2003 to address the 3,488-kilometer border dispute [c61]. Tensions rose after a 2020 clash in Galwan Valley killed 20 Indian and four Chinese soldiers [c67]. In October 2024, both sides agreed on border patrolling [c68]. That deal led to troop disengagement in eastern Ladakh [c68].

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping met in October 2024 and in 2025 [c60]. India will host the BRICS Summit on September 12, 2026 [c59]. China is building a $137-billion dam on the Brahmaputra river [c64].

vocab.meaning: a general agreement among a group
the process of moving military forces back from conflict

stories.headline: Supreme Court Judge Alleges Misconduct by Rajasthan High Court Judge
stories.body:
Supreme Court judge Justice Sandeep Mehta alleged misconduct by Rajasthan High Court Acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma [c69]. Mehta sent three letters in August 2026 to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant [c69].

Mehta alleged cases were abruptly moved to Sharma's bench without valid cause [c72]. He claimed Sharma held a meeting on a working day to designate favored lawyers as senior advocates [c73]. Mehta also cited a complaint claiming Sharma appointed personal associates to Lok Adalat positions in Jaipur and Ajmer [c81].

In addition, Mehta criticized a plan for a 100-room guest house tower as a waste of public funds [c74]. He urged the Supreme Court collegium to appoint a Chief Justice from another High Court immediately [c77].

Chief Justice Surya Kant requested a formal response from Sharma [c76]. Kant said allegations against sitting judges must follow institutional channels rather than public debate [c71].

Sharma became Acting Chief Justice in September 2025 and retires on September 26 [c70] [c75]. He was first appointed a judge in November 2016 [c78].

vocab.meaning: claims that someone has done something wrong
an official group or committee of senior judges
